fiches.contexte: A classic recipe to settle the Heart and the mind: it tonifies Qi and nourishes Yin. For restless nights, nervousness, frayed emotions, and menopausal hot flashes with night sweats.

principe.fr: Nourish the Heart, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Licorice raises blood pressure and makes the body hold on to water: avoid this dish if you have high blood pressure, swollen legs (edema), heart or kidney disease, and during pregnancy. If you take any medication (diuretics, cortisone, heart medication), ask your doctor first. No more than 2 to 3 weeks in a row. Contains gluten.

ingredients.note: In organic stores, in the grains aisle (soft wheat or spelt berries).
From a Chinese herbal shop or a specialist pharmacy. The traditional recipe uses up to 15 g; 10 g is enough at home.

etapes.texte: The day before, rinse the wheat ({ble}) and leave it to soak overnight in a large bowl of cold water.
Put the licorice ({reglisse}) in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on.
Lift out the licorice slices with a slotted spoon, or strain the decoction and pour it back into the pot.

Drain the wheat and add it to the decoction with the jujubes ({dattes}). Cook over low heat with the lid ajar, stirring now and then: the grains should burst open and the broth thicken. Add a little hot water if it runs low.
Divide between two bowls: one in the morning, one in the evening, warm. Eat the grains and the jujubes (watch out for the pits).
The day before, rinse the wheat ({ble}) and leave it to soak overnight in a large bowl of cold water.
Put the licorice ({reglisse}) in the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}), without locking the lid. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Lift out the licorice slices with a slotted spoon.
Add the drained wheat and the jujubes ({dattes}). Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Let the pressure drop on its own, then open and stir: it should be creamy. Serve in two parts, morning and evening.

notes: You can make it in the evening for the next day: it keeps 2 days in the fridge. Reheat it with a little water.
It's usually taken for 1 to 2 weeks. If sleep problems persist, talk to a practitioner.

fiches.contexte: Oysters nourish Liver and Kidney Yin and help bring down the Yang that rises to the head: headaches, dizziness, irritability, night sweats. If you have high blood pressure, this broth goes alongside your medical care, it never replaces it.

principe.fr: Nourish Yin, bring the Yang back down

fiches.precautions: Seafood allergy: avoid. The oysters must be very fresh (tightly closed shells) and cooked. Slightly cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools. If you have high blood pressure, use very little salt and keep taking your treatment.

ingredients.note: Ask your fishmonger to open them and give you the shells separately. If you have no shells: 30 g of crushed oyster shell (mu li) from a Chinese herbal shop.

etapes.texte: Open the oysters ({huitres}) over a bowl to catch their liquor. Loosen the flesh and keep it in the fridge. Scrub the empty shells under cold water.
Put the shells in a large pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on, over low heat.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and discard the shells. Add the strained oyster liquor, the soy sauce ({soja}) and the salt ({sel}), then bring back to a simmer.
Drain the oysters and roll them in the starch ({fecule}): they'll stay tender.
Slip the oysters into the simmering broth with the ginger ({gingembre}). Don't let it boil hard: they're done when their edges curl.
Off the heat, add the chives ({ciboulette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.
Open the oysters ({huitres}) over a bowl to catch their liquor. Loosen the flesh and keep it in the fridge. Scrub the empty shells under cold water.
Put the shells in the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}). Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own.
Strain the broth and discard the shells. Add the strained oyster liquor, the soy sauce ({soja}) and the salt ({sel}), then bring back to a simmer with the lid off.
Drain the oysters and roll them in the starch ({fecule}).
Slip the oysters into the simmering broth with the ginger ({gingembre}), without letting it boil hard.
Off the heat, add the chives ({ciboulette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: The oyster liquor is already salty: taste before adding salt.
The shell broth keeps 2 days in the fridge: then you only need to poach the oysters at the last minute.

fiches.contexte: A gentle soup that nourishes Yin and replenishes body fluids: for a dry mouth, thirst and constipation with dry stools. If you have diabetes, it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly or soft stools. Spinach is rich in oxalates (limit it if you get kidney stones) and in vitamin K: if you take an anticoagulant, keep the amounts steady and talk to your doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, as pale golden balls in bags.

etapes.texte: Soak the tremella ({tremelle}) in a large bowl of warm water: it will swell and soften.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base of the tremella, then tear it into small pieces. Wash the spinach ({epinards}) in plenty of water and chop it roughly.
Put the tremella in the water ({eau}) with the ginger ({gingembre}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on: it should turn tender and slightly jelly-like.
Add the spinach and cook just until it wilts.
Add salt ({sel}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}), and serve hot, with rice or bread.
Soak the tremella ({tremelle}) in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard base of the tremella and tear it into small pieces. Wash the spinach ({epinards}) and chop it roughly.
Put the tremella, water ({eau}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the pressure cooker. Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Let the pressure drop, open, add the spinach and let it simmer uncovered.
Add salt ({sel}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}), and serve hot.

notes: You can have it once or twice a day, for 3 to 4 weeks.
For a less astringent soup, blanch the spinach for 1 minute in another pot first.

fiches.contexte: A light soup that helps transform Phlegm (mucus) and clear Heat. It's also recommended for high cholesterol: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Seaweed is very rich in iodine: if you have a thyroid problem (nodule, goiter, thyroid medication), ask your doctor before eating it often. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools.

ingredients.note: The sheets used for sushi rolls (Asian aisle of supermarkets), or about 5 g of zicai seaweed cakes from Asian grocery stores.
Optional: the soup is just as good without chicken.

etapes.texte: Cut the tofu ({tofu}) into cubes and the chicken ({poulet}) into thin strips. Tear the nori ({nori}) into pieces.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the ginger ({gingembre}).
Slide the tofu into the broth and wait for it to come back to a boil. Add the chicken strips, separating them, and simmer until they're white all the way through.
Add the nori at the very end: it unfurls in a few seconds.
Add salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and drizzle with a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: Plant-based version: leave out the chicken, or replace it with a few sliced shiitake mushrooms added at the same time as the tofu.

fiches.titre: Capillary wormwood, sprouted barley and jujube soup
fiches.contexte: Capillary wormwood clears Heat and drains Dampness from the Liver; sprouted barley and jujubes look after the Spleen and Stomach. It is traditionally given for hepatitis: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Hepatitis, jaundice (yellow skin or eyes), dark urine: see your doctor first; this soup does not replace any treatment. A cooling herb: not if you have a cold belly and soft stools. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding (sprouted barley can reduce milk supply). If you take any medication, ask a practitioner for advice.

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop or a pharmacy that stocks Chinese herbs.
From the same place as the capillary wormwood.

etapes.texte: Quickly rinse the wormwood ({yinchen}), the sprouted barley ({maiya}) and the jujubes ({dattes}).
Put them in a pot with the cold water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer over low heat with the lid on.
Strain, keeping the jujubes and discarding the rest. Sweeten lightly ({sucre}) if you like.
Drink half a bowl, warm, twice a day, morning and evening, and eat the jujubes.

notes: Keep the second serving in the fridge and reheat it gently before drinking.

fiches.titre: Spring onion and fermented black soybean soup
fiches.contexte: A kitchen remedy for the very first signs of a cold caught from the cold: chills, clear runny nose, sneezing, with no thirst and no sore throat. It opens the Exterior (the outer layer of the body) to bring on a light sweat and drive out the Cold.
fiches.precautions: Only for a cold from the cold that is just starting. Not if you have a sore throat, a high fever or yellow mucus. Sweat lightly, not heavily. See a doctor if the fever rises, if you have trouble breathing or if it lasts more than 3 days. Miso is salty: go easy if you have high blood pressure.

ingredients.nom: spring onions (the white part, with the roots)

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop (dan dou chi, unsalted). Otherwise, the salted fermented black beans sold in Asian grocery stores, well rinsed.

etapes.texte: Wash the spring onions ({cebette}) well, keeping the roots. Cut the white parts into 3 cm pieces (save the green for another dish). Rinse the fermented soybeans ({douchi}).
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil, add the fermented soybeans and let them simmer.
Add the white parts of the spring onions and simmer briefly to keep their aroma.
Off the heat, dissolve the miso ({miso}) in a ladle of broth, then stir it into the pot: miso should not boil.
Drink it very hot, then cover up (sweater, blanket or comforter) and rest until you sweat lightly. Change your clothes if they're damp and stay out of drafts.

notes: You can have it 2 to 3 times during the day while the chills last; stop as soon as you've sweated a little.

fiches.titre: Lily bulb and sour jujube seed soup
fiches.contexte: An evening soup that nourishes Yin, cools the Heart and calms the mind: for insomnia, restlessness, and menopausal hot flashes with night sweats.
fiches.precautions: Only use lily bulbs sold for cooking or by herbal shops, never bulbs of garden or florist lilies. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have soft stools. Pregnancy, breastfeeding or sleep medication (sleeping pills, anti-anxiety drugs): ask a practitioner for advice.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops. Fresh (vacuum-packed, in the chilled section): use 50 g, no soaking needed.
From a Chinese herbal shop or a specialist pharmacy.

etapes.texte: The day before, soak the lily bulbs ({baihe}) in a bowl of cold water.
Roughly crush the sour jujube seeds ({zaoren}) with a mortar and pestle, or in a bag with a rolling pin.
Put the seeds in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on.
Strain the decoction through a fine sieve and discard the seeds.
Drain the lily bulbs, add them to the decoction and cook over medium heat until tender.
Drink the decoction warm and eat the bulbs, once a day, about 1 hour before bed.

notes: If you find it a little bitter, add a small piece of rock sugar at the end of cooking.

fiches.contexte: A home remedy for painful periods when the pain eases with warmth (a hot-water bottle on the belly): it warms the lower belly, disperses Cold and relieves pain.

principe.py: Wēn jīng sàn hán zhǐ tòng
principe.fr: Warm the channels, disperse Cold, relieve pain

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: not for heavy, early or bright red periods, nor if you tend to feel hot. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: ask a practitioner for advice. Don't exceed the dose and don't take it continuously. Very painful periods, periods that change, or pain that stops you from living normally need medical advice.

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop. Buy loose mugwort sold for tea, not moxa sticks.

etapes.texte: Roughly chop the mugwort ({aiye}), or put it in a cloth tea bag so no bits end up in the broth. Slice the ginger ({gingembre}).
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the mugwort and ginger, then gently lower in the eggs ({oeufs}) with a spoon. Cook at a gentle boil.
Take out the eggs, run them under cold water and peel them. Make a few small cuts in the whites so they soak up the flavor.
Put the peeled eggs back in the decoction and let them simmer.
Strain the decoction and sweeten it ({sucre}) if you like. Eat the eggs and drink the decoction very hot.

notes: Have it once a day, 5 days in a row, starting 2 to 3 days before your period is due.
During that time, keep a hot-water bottle on your lower belly and avoid iced drinks.

fiches.titre: Egg in whole cane sugar syrup
fiches.contexte: A warm treat that nourishes Blood, helps it circulate and eases belly cramps: for the 2 or 3 days after your period, for painful periods, or after giving birth.

principe.fr: Nourish Blood and help it circulate

fiches.precautions: Sweet: avoid if you have diabetes. Not during very heavy periods. After giving birth, if you have a fever, bleeding that increases or severe pain: call your midwife or doctor right away.

etapes.texte: Dissolve the sugar ({sucre}) in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil and let it bubble gently.
Beat the egg ({oeuf}) with a fork in a bowl.
Pour the egg in a thin stream into the simmering syrup, stirring gently: it forms ribbons. Let it cook.
Drink it hot, in small sips. Once a day.

notes: The sugar is reduced compared with the traditional recipe (50 g): add a little more if you like it sweeter.
If your belly feels cold, add 2 slices of fresh ginger to the syrup.
You can also poach the whole egg in the syrup (3 minutes) instead of beating it.

fiches.titre: Eggs with jujubes and goji berries
fiches.contexte: A gentle broth that nourishes the Liver and Kidney and calms the mind: for restless nights and nervousness, when the lower back and knees feel weak.

principe.fr: Tonify the Liver and Kidney, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Jujubes are sweet and rich: go easy if you have a bloated belly, mucus or diarrhea. If you take an anticoagulant, ask your doctor (goji can interact with it).

etapes.texte: Rinse the jujubes ({dattes}) and put them in a small pot with the eggs ({oeufs}) and the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then cook at a gentle boil.
Take out the eggs, run them under cold water and peel them.
Put the eggs back in the broth with the rinsed goji berries ({goji}) and let them simmer.
Eat the eggs and jujubes, and drink the broth. Once a day, ideally in the evening.

fiches.contexte: A small evening treat that nourishes Blood and Yin and calms the mind: for insomnia and nights full of dreams.
fiches.precautions: Longan is sweet and warming: go easy if you have a lot of heat (dry mouth, mouth ulcers, constipation), mucus or a bloated belly. Diabetes: in moderation and with no added sugar.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, in bags: a brown, sticky flesh, already pitted.

etapes.texte: Rinse the longan flesh ({longane}) and soak it in a little hot water.
Crack the egg ({oeuf}) into a ramekin without breaking the yolk. Sprinkle the white with sugar ({sucre}).
Steam the ramekin with the lid on until the white starts to set while the yolk is still runny.
Drain the longan and gently press it into the yolk.
Keep steaming until the egg is fully set.
Enjoy it warm, in the evening. Once a day.

notes: No steamer: set the ramekin in a pot with 2 cm of simmering water and cover.
The sugar is kept to a minimum: longan is already very sweet.

fiches.contexte: A light sweet soup that tonifies the Kidney, nourishes Essence and supports the Heart and memory. It's also recommended for high cholesterol: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Contains sugar: if you have diabetes, make it without the rock sugar. For pregnant women and young children, cook it longer until the egg yolks are fully set.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, as pale golden balls in bags.

etapes.texte: Rinse the tremella ({tremelle}) and soak it in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base, then cut the tremella into small pieces.

Put the tremella in a large heatproof bowl with the cold water ({eau}) and the rock sugar ({sucre}). Steam with the lid on until it's tender and the liquid turns slightly syrupy. Keep an eye on the water level in the steamer.
Crack the quail eggs ({oeufs}) one at a time straight into the hot soup and keep steaming.
Divide among 4 bowls, with 3 eggs each. Enjoy warm.
Rinse the tremella ({tremelle}) and soak it in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base, then cut the tremella into small pieces.
Put the tremella in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer over low heat with the lid on, stirring now and then.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and let it melt, stirring.
Crack the quail eggs ({oeufs}) one at a time into the simmering soup, without stirring.
Divide among 4 bowls, with 3 eggs each. Enjoy warm.

notes: The traditional recipe uses 100 g of rock sugar: 30 g is enough for a lightly sweet soup.
To crack a quail egg, nick the shell with the tip of a knife, then open it over a cup.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently.

fiches.contexte: Purslane clears Heat, eliminates Toxins and drains Dampness: a traditional omelet for sudden, burning, foul-smelling diarrhea.

principe.py: Qīng rè jiě dú zhǐ lì
principe.fr: Clear Heat, eliminate Toxins, stop diarrhea

fiches.precautions: Purslane is cold: not for lingering diarrhea with a cold belly, nor during pregnancy. Drink plenty to replace lost fluids. See a doctor quickly if there's a high fever, blood in the stools, diarrhea lasting more than 2 days, or if a baby or an elderly person is getting dehydrated.

ingredients.note: At markets in summer, or in the garden where it grows on its own. Pick it away from roads and wash it well.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Wash the purslane ({pourpier}) in plenty of water, drain it well and chop it finely.
Beat the eggs ({oeufs}) with the salt ({sel}), then stir in the purslane.
Heat the oil ({huile}) over medium heat in a frying pan, pour in the mixture and let it set without stirring.
Fold the omelet in half and cook a little longer, until it's set all the way through.
Serve hot, with a bowl of rice or congee.

notes: Outside of bouts of diarrhea, it's also a nice summer omelet, light and refreshing.

fiches.titre: Winter melon soup with dried shrimp
fiches.contexte: A summer soup that cools and drains Dampness: for heavy, hot days, slightly swollen legs, scanty dark urine, and that weighed-down kind of tiredness.
fiches.precautions: Shellfish allergy: replace the shrimp with 4 dried shiitake mushrooms. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly, soft stools, or if you already urinate a lot. Dried shrimp are salty: use little salt.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, often sold in slices. Peel it thinly or keep the skin, well scrubbed: it boosts the draining effect. Otherwise, use zucchini (10 min of cooking).
In Asian grocery stores, in bags.

etapes.texte: Rinse the dried shrimp ({crevettes}) and soak them in a bowl of warm water. Keep the soaking water.
Remove the seeds and spongy center of the winter melon ({courge}), then cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Put the shrimp, their soaking water, the water ({eau}) and the ginger ({gingembre}) in a pot. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Add the winter melon and simmer with the lid on until it turns translucent and meltingly soft.
Taste before adding salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and add a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}).

notes: For a stronger draining effect, add a handful of Job's tears (yi yi ren), soaked the day before, when you start the broth, and cook 20 minutes longer.

fiches.titre: Chinese cabbage soup with tofu and shiitake
fiches.contexte: A light everyday soup that is kind to the Stomach, replenishes fluids and keeps things moving: ideal after overly rich meals, or when your mouth is dry and your stools a little hard.

principe.fr: Nourish the Stomach, moisten the intestines

fiches.precautions: Rather cooling: if you have a cold belly or soft stools, double the ginger.

ingredients.note: Or 150 g of fresh shiitake, sliced, no soaking needed.

etapes.texte: Soak the shiitake ({shiitake}) in a bowl of hot water.

Drain the shiitake, keeping the water, remove the tough stems and slice the caps. Separate the white ribs of the cabbage ({chou}) from the green leaves and cut everything into strips. Cut the tofu ({tofu}) into cubes.
Put the water ({eau}), the strained soaking water, the shiitake and the ginger ({gingembre}) in a pot. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Add the white cabbage ribs and let them simmer.
Add the tofu and the green leaves, and simmer gently.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}), the spring onion ({cebette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: Add a handful of glass noodles or a little rice to the bowl to make it a full meal.
